>Accor Stadium will be the epicentre of the rugby league universe for a colossal Sunday evening showdown, as the Sydney Roosters clash with the ultimate underdog story of the year, the Newcastle Knights. The Roosters booked their Grand Final berth in style with a 36-20 victory against the Dolphins in the Preliminary Final. Meanwhile, the Knights have been the undeniable story of the finals, securing a monumental 22-14 upset over the heavily favoured Panthers in a tense Preliminary Final encounter. Riding an incredible wave of momentum, they have strung together three crucial, do-or-die victories, defying all expectations to storm from the bottom half of the eight straight into the premiership decider. The Roosters have stuck with the same squad that accounted for the Dolphins in the preliminary final to secure their first Grand Final appearance since 2019. Mark Nawaqanitawase has 5 tries in his last 3 games and is looking to sign off his NRL stint in style as he returns to rugby union. The Knights will have to do it without hooker Phoenix Crossland, who was suspended following a curse induced hip-drop tackle on Nathan Cleary, resulting in a send off. In their most recent NRL meeting, the Roosters narrowly beat the Knights 23-22 at McDonald Jones Stadium. Earlier in the 2026 campaign, the Roosters also won 38-24. Overalll, the Roosters have dominated this fixture winning 37 out of 51 H2H matches played since 1998 and have won the last six. The Roosters will be eager to maintain their attacking dominance and will benefit from a wealth of grand final experience. item.title: [ 57] Sinfest
item.description:
Fifteen years ago to the day, Tatsuya Ishida posted a strip of his webcomic that will come to mark the beginning of the decline of his webcomic Sinfest and Ishida himself. Readers thought he was setting up a new comedic arc with the new radical feminist character Xanthe — but as weeks and months came by it slowly dawned on everyone that this was the new baseline: characters lecturing the cast (and the readers) on feminist talking points.

Sinfest used to have daily threads around /co/ back then, which morphed into hateread threads and then eventually ceased to exist altogether as complaining about the state of the webcomic became just plain said to do. The webcomic's readership shrank and changed to a different demographic.

Pokémon Champions is a free to play online battle simulator available on Switch and mobile. It features ranked, casual and private battles for both singles and doubles, and will be used for VGC tournaments in 2026.

>News
- Eric Rios [ES] has won the 2027 Frankfurt Regional Championship

https://nerd-of-now.github.io/NCP-VGC-Damage-Calculator/
New Player Guide(NEW PEOPLE READ THIS):
https://rentry.org/pcg-guide (now taking suggestions and feedback)

Quick FAQ
>Do I need my own Pokémon to play?
No, the game features a recruitment system, but transferring from Home is recommended to save time and resources.
>What makes the game so much more accessible than before?
All aspects of a Pokémon are customizable with VP, a currency earned simply by playing the game. IVs are also removed.
Ask in the thread if you want any specific Pokémon, and someone will respond.
>Is there single player content?
No.
>Do I need a Nintendo Online subscription?
No.
>What's the starter pack?
US$6.99 one time purchase for 50 training tickets (fully train for free), 30 Teammate Tickets (recruit Pokemon without using VP), 50 extra box space and the LGPE trainer music. Only available on Switch for now.
>Is anything locked behind a paywall?
So far everything gameplay relevant is also purchasable with VP. Only E-Floette require ZA transfer.

item.title: [ 41] Vance tells Americans not to ‘gripe about all the little things’ as cost of living soars
item.description:
Vance tells Sean Hannity that Democratic ‘arsonists’ will reverse Trump’s successes even as he admits his own administration needs more time

https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/jd-vance-voters-midterms-gasoline-b3060535.html

Vice President JD Vance laid out the Trump administration’s best case for a Republican victory in the midterm elections on Thursday, returning to his role as the White House’s great communicator. But instead of empathizing with Americans’ economic pains and fears about the future, the vice president leaned into fear-mongering about Democrats.

Vance spoke with Fox’s Sean Hannity in an interview that aired Thursday, and leaned into the administration’s successes at driving illegal crossings at the U.S.-Mexico border to 50-year lows as he made the case for the GOP.

As he spoke about the supposed priorities of hypothetical Democratic majorities in the House and Senate, however, Vance claimed that his opponents wanted to block Republicans from ever winning elections again and “transform” America, citing such issues as acceptance of transgender Americans.

He claimed those reasons were why Americans should not “gripe” about the “little things” like gas prices nearing their Covid-era highs, U.S. casualties in the war against Iran and high cost of living issues, and give Republicans two more years to attempt to fix things.

“This is not the time to sort of gripe about all the little things. There are obviously — I think every single person who voted for us in 2024 could find something where they wish maybe congressional Republicans had gone further,” said Vance.

“But the challenge here is between Democrats who want to destroy the country, who want to permanently disempower you, make it so even if you vote Republican your vote doesn’t actually count anymore. And Republicans, who fundamentally are trying to solve the problems that Democrats under Joe Biden created. That is the choice.”

item.title: [ 33] Trump’s powerful new friends are making MAGA uncomfortable
item.description:
https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/6124669-trump-xi-mamdani-gop-concerns/

President Trump’s appearances with Chinese President Xi Jinping, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) and leaders from Silicon Valley risk turning off his political base just as Republicans are seeking to turbocharge turnout ahead of the midterms, say GOP strategists.

The president has always loved meeting with the powerful, even if they are dictators or democratic socialists, as it makes headlines and highlights his own stature.

Trump was the first president to meet with North Korea leader Kim Jong Un, and he met with Russian President Vladimir Putin last year. He had a memorable buddy-buddy term in the Oval Office with Mamdani last November, even as his party sought to vilify the liberal mayor.

To many Republicans, the latest meetings are a danger.

“Frankly, it’s inexplicable,” one unnamed Republican strategist said. “Not because as president you shouldn’t meet with the Chinese president or event the mayor of New York, but given their toxicity with the base that you were desperate to try to turnout at higher than normal levels to try and offset your vulnerabilities with every other layer of the November turnout populace.”

“You need to fire up your base and instead you’re kind of deflating them in the homestretch,” the strategist added.

Trump hosted his Chinese counterpart last week for a lavish state visit at the White House. That meeting came after Mamdani hosted Trump at Gracie Mansion in New York City.

On Tuesday, Trump invited several tech leaders to the White House for a luncheon on artificial intelligence before appearing with them on the White House North Lawn for an impromptu news conference.

Polling shows that the president’s base views China with skepticism.

item.title: [ 65] Cheap generic table salt contains toxic cyanide as an anti-caking agent
item.description:
They call it "Yellow Prussiate of Soda" but it is just a fancy name for "Sodium ferrocyanide". I noticed that only the cheapest generic brands of table salt use this. The quality name brands like Morton instead use benign Calcium Silicate as its anti-caking ingredient.

Its not like salt is really very expensive either way. But the generic stuff is somewhat cheaper, but its not really a big deal either way in my opinion. But this is what you end up getting in exchange for that marginally cheaper price.

If you look that stuff up in the wikipedia article it says it is particularly damaging to your kidneys. But government regulators say its "okay" because not much of it is being used. Well, I don't know about that. I'd prefer to keep my kidneys in good working order, thank you very much.

Just pay like $1 more for the good salt. Its a small price to pay to not end up having kidney failure later in life and having to go through dialysis or whatever.

item.title: [123] Moving to England
item.description:
How bad of an idea would it be for an American to attempt to move to England? I'm finishing graduate school soon, and I don't want to look for a job in the US. I've visited England 6 times, but what is it like to actually live here?

My main motivation is the public transport. I absolutely fucking hate driving. It terrifies me. I don't understand why something so dangerous and so expensive is widely accepted as being a necessity for everyday life. It is ruining my life, because my country has no good public transport.

Many other European countries have good public transport, but I only speak English. Would I regret moving here? I love English people, and have several close friends who live there. I would only want to live somewhere that I can actually meet people, so no rural hamlets.

Original filename: 01-England-Outline.jpg

item.title: [ 71] Ever been impressed with how disappointing something is in real life? And I don
item.description:
Ever been impressed with how disappointing something is in real life? And I don't mean the obvious tourist traps like Plymouth Rock where it's pretty clear there's nothing to see. I mean ones that can look cool in a decent picture.

I'd seen the Supertrees hyped up online for years. People saying only Singapore could do this and the whole world is behind back when these things were first presented. Though they must be pretty impressive.

Turns out it just feels like a cheap amusement park attraction within a fairly mid park. It's tacky pink and neon green plastic piping with vines that only go up partway.

item.title: [225] Places you got memed into
item.description:
>look for a cheap place to stay while visa times reset
>insanely cheap from checking out online, lots of places 24/7, train up and down the country, and english spoken
>why the fuck does no one talk about this place? I think I saw some people on trv talk about it once
>book in KL
Holy shit I did not think it possible for something to be less soulless than fucking Seoul. The air sucks, the food portions suck, the weather sucks, the "local transportation" is ass, everyone smells like sewage or curry, you run through things and then it's just "mall mall mall hey did you want to check out that small attraction at the mall?" from anyone you meet. Bars are just awful filled with obvious chinese scammers or old fucks from UK, sometimes passing business people. Try to look online for interesting things, you can blow out KL in like 2.5 weeks of going out, and everyone just says "never run out of things,,," and don't get me started at 5AM singing.

Is there any saving grace for this place?
